W3 (cost lens), after E037.

**Tip (E036).** 231 steps at batch 2000. Resolutions 20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30% of steps. Stem frozen at 75%, whitening output detached from step 46. Measured 5.314 s and 0.7532, which sits exactly on the 0.753 bar.

**E037: freeze moved from 75% to 60%.** It saved 0.25 s (−4.6%) and lost 0.38 pp on the 3-seed mean. That is about 0.65 s/pp, worse than the epoch dial. The 60–75% band carries group-1 feature learning, so the freeze-dose curve is steep below 75%.

**Code facts:**
- Muon renormalizes filters and has no wd, so filter wd is inert.
- Newton-Schulz runs 3 iterations.
- Group-1 BN runs at 15×15 after the pool. The large-map work is conv1's 31×31×128 output and the pool.
- After 20% of steps the whitening has no backward.

**Time budget.** Time ≈ F (about 0.25 s) + Σ steps × per-step cost.
- Per step: about 0.032 s at 32 px, 0.026 at 28, 0.021 at 24, 0.016 at 20, minus the detach and freeze savings.
- 0.5 epoch ≈ 0.3 s.
- Memory-bound savings have come in at or above face value every time (E028, E031, E034, E036, E037). My time forecasts have hit for 6 runs in a row.

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost):**
- Epoch dial: 1.5–2.5.
- Freeze at 75%: about 2.
- Early low resolution: 1–2.
- Whitening detach: ≥1.
- Freeze 75%→60%: about 0.65 (bad).
- Width cut: about 0.7 (bad).
- Loss-based dropping: about 2.

**Accuracy boosters.** Every schedule and regularization tweak was ≤0 on held-out seeds (E025, E029, E030, E032). Prior for untested ones: −0.2 ± 0.25 pp. Only steps and Muon reliably buy accuracy, and Muon is still unconfounded.

**Mechanisms:**
1. Lookahead averaging is worth about 1 pp and is already tuned (E005, E025, E030).
2. Muon is worth about 0.3–0.6 pp at about 3% time (E006).
3. Accuracy is built at 28/32 px and needs a trainable stem through about 75% of steps (E011, E018, E024, E033, E037).
4. Large-map backward is bandwidth-bound (E028, E034, E036).
5. An RNG re-draw moves the 3-seed mean by ±0.1–0.3 pp (E035).

**Noise:**
- Per-seed std about 0.3 pp; 3-seed SE about 0.17 pp; 10-seed SE about 0.1 pp.
- Time noise about 1%.
- A committed recipe re-run reproduces bit-identically (E012, E019).

**Remaining budget.** Little cheap time is left in the stem. BN folding at 15×15 is worth ≤1%. The remaining candidates are the architecture of group-1 conv1 at 31×31, batch per phase (H5.1.3), and dropping Muon only if E006 was confounded.

**Unsure:**
- The tip's true population mean. I estimate 0.752–0.7535 after the winner's curse. That is above the 40-seed bar of 0.75, but any further trim needs accuracy bought back first.
- Whether the PCIe judge discounts bandwidth-bound savings.

forecasts.reason: No recipe change, so seeds 0–2 should reproduce. The pooled 20-seed mean will likely land around 0.7525–0.753 with the winner's curse, a coin flip against the ≥0.753 bar.
Group-1 BN runs at 15×15, so folding it saves BN reductions on only about 58 steps: roughly 0.02–0.04 s, well short of 2%. Eval-mode BN during training risks a small accuracy loss.
E028 and E036 imply large-map work is bandwidth-heavy. Non-GEMM ≥30% and whitening plus group 1 ≥35% of the full 32 px step are both likely.
Dropping Newton-Schulz saves about 2–3%. SGD at batch 2000 with ported scaling is untuned for this short schedule, so a loss of ≥0.3 pp is likely.

cruxes: What is the tip's true population mean (pooled seeds 3–22)? If it is ≥0.7535, a 0.25-epoch trim of about 0.15 s is affordable; if not, the next cut first needs accuracy bought back.
Is Muon worth ≥0.3 pp unconfounded (I059)? If not, dropping it is about 3% of free time.

In the profile, what share of the 32 px and 20/24 px steps goes to group-1 conv1 at 31×31 and to per-step overhead (Muon, Lookahead, launches)? This decides whether any non-schedule lever worth ≥3% remains.
